findings.title: Materials' earnings rebound is being ignored
findings.body: Materials trades at a forward P/E of 17.15 but a trailing P/E of 35.85, a 52 percent compression implying 109 percent earnings growth. The forward percentile is only 37 while trailing sits at 86, so the market is not paying up for the rebound — it is discounting that the surge is transient.

findings.title: Utilities' trailing cheapness is a red flag
findings.body: Utilities has a forward P/E of 17.50 at percentile 28 versus a trailing percentile of 2. The 26-point gap between the lenses is driven by a mere 4 percent expected earnings growth, meaning analysts see little earnings power ahead despite the historically depressed reported figures.

findings.title: Health Care hits a valuation ceiling
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E of 20.35 sits at the 100th percentile of its five-year range, yet the market still assumes 80 percent earnings growth. The 45 percent compression from trailing to forward shows analysts underwriting a margin expansion that has no room left to be rewarded at this multiple.
